chief_complaint: profound anhedonia, psychomotor retardation, feelings of worthlessness, and terminal insomnia for 3 months
hpi_details: 45F reports 3 months of persistent, severe low mood present most of the day, every day. Has lost interest in playing piano and reading (anhedonia). Wakes up every morning at 03:00 AM and cannot fall back asleep (terminal insomnia). Experiences profound fatigue, feeling that 'moving my limbs requires walking through wet cement.' Expresses intense guilt over past minor mistakes, difficulty concentrating at work, and passive suicidal ideation ('wishing I would just not wake up tomorrow') without active intent or plan.
ideas: thinks she is a complete failure as a mother and employee
concerns: worried she will never feel normal again or experience joy
expectations: wants medication to help her sleep and lift the heavy mental cloud
pmh: Major Depressive Disorder (one prior episode 8 years ago treated with Sertraline)

clinical_knowledge.topic: Major Depressive Disorder evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Major Depressive Disorder is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Standard management emphasizes Outpatient management with close safety monitoring (or voluntary admission if safety/support inadequate), adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: profound anhedonia, psychomotor retardation, feelings of worthlessness, and terminal insomnia for 3 months

Key HPI features: 45F reports 3 months of persistent, severe low mood present most of the day, every day. Has lost interest in playing piano and reading (anhedonia). Wakes up every morning at 03:00 AM and cannot fall back asleep (terminal insomnia). Experiences profound fatigue, feeling that 'moving my limbs requires walking through wet cement.' Expresses intense guilt over past minor mistakes, difficulty concentrating at work, and passive suicidal ideation ('wishing I would just not wake up tomorrow') without active intent or plan.

Objective/Exam findings: Vitals: HR 72, BP 118/76. Psychomotor retardation evident with slow movements, downcast gaze, and long latencies in speech responses. Affect is severely depressed and tearful. PHQ-9 score 22/27 (Severe Depression). Columbia Suicide Severity Rating Scale (C-SSRS) confirms passive ideation (Category 2) without active formulation, preparation, or intent. Baseline CBC, CMP, and TSH normal.
Relevant background/PMH: Major Depressive Disorder (one prior episode 8 years ago treated with Sertraline)
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Major Depressive Disorder.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Bipolar depression without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Active suicidal ideation with plan.
management_principles: Outpatient management with close safety monitoring (or voluntary admission if safety/support inadequate)
Discuss evidence-based psychotherapy and, after assessing bipolar history, contraindications, and patient preference, consider an SSRI with close follow-up
Educate patient on 2-4 week latency before mood benefits appear and black box warning regarding suicidal ideation monitoring
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: 45F presenting with major depressive episode featuring melancholic features (terminal insomnia, psychomotor retardation, profound anhedonia) and passive suicidal ideation.
reference_soap.objective: Vitals: HR 72, BP 118/76. Psychomotor retardation evident with slow movements, downcast gaze, and long latencies in speech responses. Affect is severely depressed and tearful. PHQ-9 score 22/27 (Severe Depression). Columbia Suicide Severity Rating Scale (C-SSRS) confirms passive ideation (Category 2) without active formulation, preparation, or intent. Baseline CBC, CMP, and TSH normal.
reference_soap.assessment: Major Depressive Disorder, Recurrent, Severe without psychotic features (Melancholic Specifier).
reference_soap.plan: Complete a collaborative suicide risk assessment, including intent, plan, access to means, protective factors, and ability to follow a safety plan. Arrange urgent emergency assessment or admission if active intent, a plan, inability to maintain safety, psychosis, or inadequate support emerges; otherwise arrange close follow-up, a written safety/crisis plan, and psychotherapy. After assessing bipolar history, contraindications, and patient preference, consider an SSRI and counsel on delayed benefit and early changes in suicidal thinking.

learning_objectives: Apply DSM-5 criteria (SIGECAPS) for Major Depressive Disorder and recognize melancholic specifiers (early morning awakening, psychomotor slowing, anhedonia)
Conduct standardized suicide risk assessment utilizing the Columbia Suicide Severity Rating Scale (C-SSRS) distinguishing passive vs active ideation
Select appropriate first-line antidepressant therapy (SSRIs/SNRIs) and counsel regarding onset latency and early activating side effects
Outline evidence-based psychotherapy integration (CBT/Interpersonal Therapy) with pharmacotherapy

teaching.one_liner: Persistent depressed mood and pervasive anhedonia lasting at least two weeks, severely impairing daily psychosocial functioning.
red_flags: Inability to collaborate on a safety plan or lack of a safe support environment

must_ask.objective: Mood and anhedonia specific to lost hobbies
must_ask.say: Have you lost interest in playing piano or reading, things you used to enjoy?
Do you wake up very early, around 3 in the morning, and find you can't fall back asleep?
Do you feel like moving or even walking takes tremendous effort, or feel guilty about past mistakes?
Have you had thoughts of dying or hurting yourself? Have you thought about how you would do it, have access to means, or feel you might act on it?

must_ask.objective: Prior manic or hypomanic episode screening
must_ask.say: Have you ever had a period of unusually high energy or barely needing sleep?

history.answer: I've been feeling so deeply depressed for the past few months, and I just have no energy or motivation to do anything.
It started gradually about three months ago, and the low mood has been there almost all day, every single day without relief.
There was no specific tragedy, bereavement, or job loss; it just slowly crept over me without a clear trigger.
I completely lost interest in playing the piano and reading, which were the two things that used to bring me the greatest happiness.
I fall asleep okay, but I wake up abruptly every morning around 3:00 AM and find myself staring at the ceiling unable to get back to sleep.
Food has completely lost its taste to me, so I have to force myself to eat and I have lost about four kilograms over these three months.
I feel an overwhelming exhaustion every day, as if just moving my arms and legs requires walking through wet cement.
My thoughts feel terribly cloudy and slow, so I have a lot of trouble concentrating at the library and making simple decisions.
I feel completely worthless and constantly dwell on small mistakes I made years ago, blaming myself for everything.
My husband noticed that my speech has become noticeably slow, and every movement feels heavy and delayed.
I catch myself wishing that I simply would not wake up the next morning, but I haven't done anything to hurt myself.
No, I don't have any plan, method, or intention to end my life; I could never do that to my family.
My two children and my husband are everything to me, and knowing how much they love and need me keeps me going.
I am falling behind on cataloging books at work, and at home I can barely manage to cook dinner or fold laundry.
No, I have never had a period where I felt unusually high, energetic, or able to stay awake for days without feeling tired.
No, I don't hear voices or see things that other people cannot, and I don't feel that anyone is spying on me or plotting against me.
I don't drink alcohol, and I don't take sleeping medications or any illegal substances.
No, I haven't felt unusually cold, my bowels are regular, and I haven't started taking any new prescription medications.
No, my youngest child is ten years old, and I have not had a baby or been pregnant recently.
I had a severe depressive episode about eight years ago, but it completely cleared up after my doctor treated me with sertraline.
My maternal aunt struggled with depression, but there is no family history of bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, or suicide.
Other than the depressive episode eight years ago, I've always been physically healthy with no chronic medical issues.
I had an uncomplicated appendectomy twenty years ago, and both of my children were delivered through normal, uncomplicated hospital births.
I am not taking any prescription drugs, over-the-counter remedies, or herbal supplements right now.
I don't have any known allergies to medicines, foods, or anything in the environment.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used any tobacco or nicotine products in my life.
I work as a community librarian, and I live in an apartment with my husband and our two school-aged children.
My periods come regularly every twenty-eight days, my last one started two weeks ago, and there is no possibility of pregnancy.
I keep thinking that this is all my fault and that I'm just a complete failure as a mother and at my job.
I'm terrified that this dark cloud is permanent and that I will never feel normal or experience real joy ever again.
I am hoping you can prescribe a medication to help me sleep through the night and help lift this heavy mental cloud.

exam.finding: Blood pressure is 118/76 mmHg, pulse is 72 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 14 breaths per minute, temperature is 36.8°C, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air.
Shows noticeable psychomotor retardation with slowed body movements, stooped posture, downcast gaze, poor eye contact, and a visibly weary, tearful appearance.

Speech exhibits prolonged latencies and low volume; affect is severely depressed and tearful; PHQ-9 score is 22/27; C-SSRS confirms passive suicidal ideation without plan or intent; orientation, cognition, and insight are intact.
Thyroid gland is normal in size, non-tender, smooth, and without palpable nodules, masses, or thyromegaly.
Conjunctivae are pink without pallor, and sclerae are anicteric.
Heart sounds S1 and S2 are normal with regular rhythm and rate, and no murmurs, gallops, or friction rubs are heard.
Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally with vesicular breath sounds and no crackles, wheezes, or rhonchi.
Deep tendon reflexes are 2+ and symmetric throughout with normal relaxation speed, and plantar reflexes are down-going.
Skin is warm, dry, and intact with normal turgor, no cutaneous myxedema, and no signs of self-inflicted trauma.
